points.description: States that empirical equations are derived from experiments, observations or measured/observed data (not from theory).
points.partial_credit: Half if vague, e.g. 'based on practice/experience' without mentioning experiments or observed data.

points.description: States that they have no mathematical/theoretical proof or derivation behind them (they are not derived from theory/first principles).
points.partial_credit: Half if only implied or vaguely stated, e.g. 'not exact' or 'approximate' without saying no theoretical proof.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need both ideas: equations come from experiments/observed data, and they lack a mathematical or theoretical proof. Give 1 mark if only one idea is clearly stated, or both are stated vaguely. Give 0 for wrong or unrelated answers, such as saying they are derived from theory or proven mathematically.
